analysis.title: Europe Open - Cruise control
key_insights: A record tech IPO lifted Nasdaq futures about 1.6-2% overnight and points to a stronger open for European equities, but Asia sentiment stayed weak. Taiex led losses, down 4%, on jitters over APEC summit takeaways.

Hang Seng is weaker after Tencent earnings. Management warned that US curbs on Chinese access to overseas data centers should slow short-run AI model training, which weighed on Chinese model names (Minimax down 9%, Z.AI down 6%).
Australian bonds rallied sharply after the unemployment rate rose 0.2pp to 4.9% and employment fell 43.5k (Citi forecast 35k, consensus 20k). Citi economists see a looser underlying labor market.
Citi expects the RBA cash rate to stay at 4.85% until Q3 2027. Another hike remains possible but needs stronger inflation surprises.
USTs followed the AU rally, but momentum stalled into the London open. Citi traders saw fast money buying in the 5y and 30y sectors.

The Oct FOMC showed most officials expected further hikes despite the pause. Citi calls a 25bp hike in Dec highly likely and a consecutive hike in Jan plausible. Citi economists do not expect aggressive hikes if sentiment deteriorates materially and financial conditions tighten substantially.
AUDUSD fell as low as 0.6662 before recovering to 0.67. Asia session volume in the pair was 2.1x higher according to eTrading. G10 pairs otherwise traded in tight ranges, with USDJPY near 159.6.

Citi FX is selling AUDJPY rallies, with 106 as the first target after an attempt to break it. It also favors selling EURJPY rallies and is watching a weekly close below 175, the 2024 high and 100-week moving average. The options desk likes owning convexity as USDJPY approaches 160.
BoJ's Ueda said the BoJ is watching the impact of global central bank tightening, with wage hikes spreading. This leaves the door open for a rate hike next month, in line with market expectations.
RBNZ Governor Breman flagged two-sided inflation risks and an uneven recovery, with export-focused parts of the economy stronger than expected.
Trump said he would not ask Xi or Putin for help on Iran and wants a lasting deal with Iran. Oil drifted and gold recovered above $3700 while the trilateral meeting was under way.

BoE's Dhingra speaks at 12:15 GMT and is expected to lean dovish. Oct CPI did not firm up a Dec hike, which is still priced heavily (20bp). Citi economists saw minimal evidence of second-round effects.

SARB is expected to deliver a hawkish hold, though Citi says a 25bp hike would help stabilize sentiment. Citi strategists see scope for another move in January depending on oil prices and diesel spreads. ZAR fell more than 2% on Wednesday following gold.
Banxico minutes follow a 3-2 split decision to cut the policy rate 25bp to 6.25%. The last time similar 'extended period' language was used, the rate stayed unchanged for almost a year.
Malaysia Oct CPI printed at 1.9% y/y against 2.0% consensus and 1.8% prior.
